protocol.name: cupertino_host_v1

description.summary: private protocol between the Cupertino server, a shell host and its components

protocol.description:
A shell host is a process that runs components of the shell, each on a thread and a connection of its own. The server starts the host on a connection that holds the host role and nothing else, tells it which components it runs, and hands it one connection per component on request; a component's roles are bound to that connection and end with it. The host reports what it observes of each component (busy, unresponsive, lost, failed), and the server decides what follows: when a component starts again, when it stops, and which host runs it. A component holds its roles in one host at a time.
The protocol is private and unstable: interfaces may change without a version bump.

interface.name: cupertino_host_v1

description.summary: a shell host

interface.description:
Global singleton, offered only to a connection the server made for a host process it started. The connection holds the host role alone: it sees this global and the core globals, and none of the roles of the components.
Right after binding the server sends kind, then the component list: one component event for each component this host runs, followed by done. Whenever the list changes the whole list is sent again, and each list replaces the one before. For a component of the list the host creates its object with get_component and asks for its connection. A component that left the list is stopped by the host, which then destroys its object.
A host is shared or separate. The shared host runs every component that no separate host runs, and serves the host bus, the message bus of the components, on a socket of its own (serve_bus). A separate host runs one component and reaches the host bus through that socket (bus). A session has at most one shared host; while components run, it has exactly one, also when its list is empty.

entry.name: component
entry.summary: the host already holds an object for that component

entry.name: kind
entry.summary: a request only the shared host may make came from a separate one

entry.name: path
entry.summary: the bus socket path is not absolute or is over 107 bytes

entry.name: shared
entry.summary: runs the components no separate host runs and serves the host bus

entry.name: separate
entry.summary: runs one component and reaches the host bus through the shared host

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the host global

request.description: Component objects created through this global stay valid.

event.name: kind

description.summary: what this host is

event.description: Sent once, before the first list.

event.name: component

description.summary: a component this host runs

event.description: The name is one of the server's component table (at most 32 bytes of lower-case ASCII letters). The components sent since the last done are the whole list. A name the host does not hold a component for is answered with get_component and unavailable.

event.name: done

description.summary: end of a component list

event.description: A list may be empty: the host then runs no component. A separate host whose list is empty exits successfully once its component has stopped.

request.name: get_component

description.summary: the host's object for one component

request.description: Creates the object the host reports the component's state on and receives its connection on. A name that is not in the host's current list is not an error, since the list may have just changed: the object is inert, its connect is never answered, and the host destroys it when the next list arrives without the name. Posts the component error when the host already holds an object for the name.

request.name: request_restart

description.summary: ask to be restarted at a quiet moment

request.description: The host holds a thread it cannot end (a component that was lost) and asks to be started afresh. The server answers with restart once the seat has had no input for two seconds and no component of this host holds a grab or shows a transient surface. A restart asked for this way is not counted as a crash of the host. Asking again before the answer changes nothing.

event.name: restart

description.summary: the quiet moment came

event.description: The answer to request_restart: the host stops its components and exits. The server starts it again at once, with the list it has then. The persistent surfaces of its components are held meanwhile (cupertino_component_v1.persist).

request.name: serve_bus

description.summary: where the shared host serves the host bus

request.description: The absolute path of a listening Unix stream socket in the runtime directory that the shared host made (mode 0600). The server passes it to every separate host. Sent again when the host serves another socket; the earlier path is then void. Posts the kind error from a separate host and the path error for a path that is not absolute or is over 107 bytes.

event.name: bus_peer

description.summary: a separate host may join the host bus

event.description: Sent to the shared host for each separate host, after serve_bus and again after each later serve_bus: the separate host that runs component may connect to the socket and present token, 32 lower-case hexadecimal digits the server drew at random. The shared host accepts a token once and accepts no connection without one.

event.name: bus_peer_gone

description.summary: a separate host ended

event.description: The token of the separate host that ran component is void, and the shared host closes the connection it made with it.

event.name: bus

description.summary: where a separate host reaches the host bus

event.description: Sent to a separate host once the shared host serves the bus, and again whenever it serves another socket: connect to path and present token. Until it arrives, and while no shared host runs, the component's messages to other components wait in the separate host.

interface.name: cupertino_host_component_v1

description.summary: one component, as its host sees it

interface.description:
The host asks for the component's connection with connect and starts the component when connection arrives. While the component runs, the host watches whether its loop returns to its wait and reports busy, unresponsive, responsive and lost. When the component ends without being asked to, the host reports failed and asks for a connection again; the server decides when it comes.
The server keeps the component's failures: they outlive this object and the host. A component that failed starts again no sooner than 0.25 seconds after the failure, a time that doubles with each failure up to 8 seconds and starts over once the component ran for 60 seconds. Five failures within 60 seconds stop it (stopped) until the person asks for a restart or logs in again.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: give the component up

request.description: Sent once the component has stopped, when a list leaves it out or the host exits. The server closes the component's connection if it is open.

request.name: connect

description.summary: ask for the component's connection

request.description: The host has no running instance of the component and is ready to start one. The server first closes any connection it holds for the component in this host, then answers with connection when the component may start, or with stopped. One answer is outstanding at most: asking again before it arrives changes nothing.

event.name: connection

description.summary: the component's connection

event.description: The client end of a connection that holds the component's roles and no other, valid while this host process lives. The host starts the component on it. The descriptor is close-on-exec and must stay so: no child of the host inherits it.

event.name: stopped

description.summary: the component stays stopped

event.description: Sent in place of connection: the server starts the component no more by itself. The persistent surfaces the server held for it are released. A connection event follows when the person asks for a restart of the component.

event.name: restart

description.summary: stop the component and start it again

event.description: The person asked for a restart of the component while it runs: the host stops it, as for a component that leaves the list, and sends connect. Not counted as a failure.

request.name: busy

description.summary: the component's loop has not returned to its wait

request.description: The host's watchdog found the component's loop out of its wait at one of its checks (every 0.5 seconds, after a start-up grace of 10 seconds). The server stops waiting for the component where it would: a transaction that expects it starts without it.

request.name: unresponsive

description.summary: the component has been busy for two seconds

request.description: The server releases the component's grabs, dismisses its transient surfaces, returns the keyboard focus to the window that had it and sends the component no input. Its persistent surfaces keep their place and their picture.

request.name: responsive

description.summary: the component's loop is back in its wait

request.description: Ends busy and unresponsive: the component gets input again, and what it shows from then is shown.

request.name: lost

description.summary: the component has been busy for ten seconds

request.description: The host has shut the component's sockets down and keeps its thread, which it cannot end. The server holds the component's persistent surfaces, takes the component out of this host's list and starts it alone in a separate host, where it stays for the rest of the session or until the person asks for a restart of the component. A shared host follows with request_restart.

entry.name: panic
entry.summary: the component, one of its tasks or one of its helper threads panicked

entry.name: error
entry.summary: its loop ended with an error: a protocol error or a connection that closed

entry.name: exit
entry.summary: its loop returned without being asked to stop

request.name: failed

description.summary: the component ended without being asked to

request.description: The host has torn the component down and shut its sockets. The server counts the failure, whatever its cause, and holds the component's persistent surfaces. Posts the cause error for a value that is not an entry of failure.

request.name: unavailable

description.summary: this host has no such component

request.description: The host was built without the component. The server leaves it stopped in this host and logs it; it is not counted as a failure.

interface.name: cupertino_component_v1

description.summary: what a component tells the server about itself

interface.description: Global singleton, offered only on a connection the server handed out through cupertino_host_component_v1.connection. Right after binding the server sends component, then one hold event for each surface it holds from the component's earlier instance, followed by done.

entry.name: invalid_surface
entry.summary: the surface belongs to another client, is gone or is not a layer shell surface

entry.name: mapped
entry.summary: the surface already committed a buffer

entry.name: key
entry.summary: a key that is empty, over 64 bytes, or already names another surface of the connection

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the global

request.description: The announced bus name and the persistent surfaces stay as they are.

event.name: component

description.summary: the component this connection belongs to

event.description: The name of the component whose roles the connection holds.

event.name: hold

description.summary: a surface held from the earlier instance

event.description: The server keeps the last picture and the reserved space of a persistent surface of this component whose connection ended. key is the key that surface was persisted with.

description.summary: end of the holds

request.name: announce_bus_name

description.summary: the component's connection to the session bus

request.description: The unique name (":1.42") of the bus connection the component owns its well-known names on. The server asks the bus daemon for the process behind that name and accepts it when it is the host process this connection was handed to; the answer is bus_name. From then on the server takes a bus call from that name as this component's, and a call from another connection of the same process as not this component's. Announcing again replaces the name. Posts the name error for a string that is not a unique bus name.

entry.name: accepted
entry.summary: the name belongs to this component's host

entry.name: refused
entry.summary: the name belongs to another process, or the bus did not answer in time

event.name: bus_name

description.summary: the answer to announce_bus_name

event.description: Sent once for each announcement. A refused name leaves the component without a bus identity: the server treats its bus calls as an unknown caller's.

request.name: persist

description.summary: make a layer shell surface persistent

request.description:
A surface is transient unless it is persisted. When the component's connection ends, or the component is reported unresponsive, the server dismisses its transient surfaces at once. A persistent surface is held instead when the connection ends: its last picture stays where it is with its reserved space, every animation of its layers at its end, and takes no input.
key names the surface among the component's persistent surfaces on its output and is the same for each instance of the component. When this connection persists a surface with the key of a hold on the same output, that surface takes the hold over: with its first commit that attaches a buffer, in the same frame, the held picture goes and the surface shows in its place, and the reserved space passes to it without the usable area changing in between.
Sent before the surface's first commit that attaches a buffer. Posts invalid_surface for a surface that is not a layer shell surface of this client, mapped for one that already committed a buffer, and key for an empty key, one over 64 bytes or one another surface of the connection has on the same output.

request.name: ready

description.summary: the component has shown what it shows at start

request.description: Every hold of the earlier instance that no surface took over ends: its picture goes and its space is given back. Without this request the server ends those holds 10 seconds after it handed the connection out. A restart the person asked for is answered when this request arrives.
